title: Rigidification detects categorical equivalences
statement: Use simplicial sets [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set], simplicial categories as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and categorical equivalences in the testing convention of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]: $f:S\to T$ is such an equivalence when $h\operatorname{Fun}(T,Z)\to h\operatorname{Fun}(S,Z)$ is an equivalence for every quasicategory $Z$ in a sufficiently large universe. For $n\geq0$, define $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ with objects $0,\ldots,n$ and mapping simplicial set from $i$ to $j$ for $i\leq j$ the ordinary nerve of the poset of subsets of $\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing both endpoints, ordered by inclusion; the mapping set is empty for $i>j$. Composition is union of subsets. A monotone map induces the enriched functor given by image of subsets. For every simplicial set $S$, put $\mathfrak C[S]=\operatorname{colim}_{\Delta^n\to S}\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, with colimit in $\mathrm{sCat}$. Then for every simplicial map $f:S\to T$, $\mathfrak C[f]$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-cell-stability] if and only if $f$ is a categorical equivalence.
